questions.question: When does a `finally` block run?
options: Only if the try block throws an error
Only if the try block succeeds without errors
Always — regardless of whether the try block succeeds, throws, or executes a return statement
Only if there is no catch block present
questions.explanation: finally is guaranteed to run no matter what happens in try/catch, which is why it's the right place for unconditional cleanup.

questions.question: What is the benefit of extending the built-in `Error` class to create a custom error type?
options: It makes the error disappear from stack traces
It preserves proper stack traces and instanceof Error behavior, while letting you attach extra context and distinguish error types with instanceof
It is required for try/catch to work at all
Custom error classes cannot carry any extra data
questions.explanation: Extending Error keeps standard error behavior intact while allowing custom properties (like a field name) and type-checking via instanceof.

questions.question: What is the key difference between an "operational error" and a "programmer error"?
options: There is no meaningful difference; all errors should be handled the same way
Operational errors are expected failure modes (bad input, network timeout) that should be caught and handled; programmer errors are bugs that generally should not be silently swallowed
Programmer errors only happen in development, never in production
Operational errors cannot be caught with try/catch
questions.explanation: Distinguishing expected failures from actual bugs matters because silently catching programmer errors (e.g. with an empty catch block) hides real problems instead of surfacing them.

questions.question: Why is an empty `catch {}` block generally considered an anti-pattern?
options: It's a syntax error in modern JavaScript
It swallows both operational errors AND programmer errors alike, silently hiding real bugs instead of letting them be noticed and fixed
catch blocks must always log something by specification
questions.explanation: An empty catch block suppresses all errors indiscriminately, including genuine bugs that should have surfaced loudly rather than vanished silently.
